decisions.reason: The first Remark incorrectly makes the whole centre connected and trivial: for G=SL2 over C and n=0, H=G and Z(H)=mu2. The proof itself only needs and correctly proves triviality of the identity component, finiteness of the full centre, and vanishing of its Lie algebra in characteristic zero. Corrected the Remark without changing the Statement or Proof.

Original steps 1.1-2.1 attributed root-group restrictions and coroot pairings to F3 although its cited Statement supplies only central-kernel representation descent. Thus dominance of the pulled-back weight, needed for F2, was unsupported. Repaired locally from root-group, scheme-image, diagonalizable, and Borel suppliers: root-group kernel intersections vanish, images identify roots, rank-one reflections identify coroot pairings, and compatible product Borels give dominance before existence and descent.

reviews.reason: Reviewed all seven proof steps: Jacobi gives a commutative ambient ideal and its ideal centralizer; the pointwise basis stabilizer realizes that centralizer. Cartier and the normality supplier make H identity component normal. Geometric centralizers and smoothness identify the adjoint kernel with the centre and Lie Z(H identity component) with Z(h); its identity component lies in R(G)=1, so n lies in the zero Lie centre. The corrected Remark now says finite centre, not trivial centre. Milne printed p.477, lines 24328-24336, agrees. Statement, AC qualification, owning contract derivations and page interface are unchanged. This is a local repair review, not independent review of my edit.

Reviewed the repaired seven-step proof and actual cited supplier interfaces. The central kernel is in T_H, its intersection with each root group is trivial as a unipotent subgroup of a torus, and the exact image supplier gives smooth root-group images. Kernel-trivial root characters descend by the diagonalizable anti-equivalence; one-dimensional tangent weights and the containment criterion identify root images, with equal dimensions giving bijection. Torus pullback intertwines rank-one reflections, giving exact coroot pairings. Positive systems and the cocharacter Borel decomposition identify B_H with a product Borel mapping to B. Dominance then licenses the product primitive vector, generated simple quotient, central-isogeny descent and finite dimensionality; both equivalent formulations follow. Nonreduced finite kernels, pure tori and zero coroot pairings remain included. Statement unchanged, no new prerequisite item needed. This is a local repair review, not independent review of my repair.
